transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-01
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Rafael Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Quantilytics Head of Data), Samir Patel (Quantilytics Platform Eng), Elena Gomez (ML Lead)

Summary:
Quick scoping call to pick an open-model shortlist for the POC, define success criteria (latency/cost/quality), confirm workload sizing and benchmarks, and align on timeline + security needs. Redwood AE + SE present to advise on models and test harness.

Topics covered:
- POC goals and success criteria
- Workload sizing (tokens/sec, concurrent requests)
- Benchmark metrics (p50/p95 latency, throughput, cost per 1k tokens, quality evals)
- Open-model shortlist and quality vs cost tradeoffs
- Multilingual and domain-specific considerations (financial analytics)
- Security/compliance (SOC2, VPC, KMS)
- Next steps and owners

Transcript body:
00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, and with me is Rafael, our Solutions Engineer. How's everyone doing?
00:06 Priya: Good thanks, Priya here. We've been looking at open models primarily, want to run a cost-conscious POC for our financial reporting assistant.
00:12 Rafael: Great, can you give a sense of traffic and SLOs — do you need sub-200ms p50 or is p95 more important?
00:18 Priya: For interactive queries p50 around 200-300ms is fine, but p95 should be under 1.5s ideally, we can tolerate some tail as long as throughput is predictable.
00:31 Elena: Also the model needs to be strong on financial language and multi-lingual — we have reports in English, Spanish and Portuguese.
00:38 Samir: From infra, we'll probably start with a small pilot: 10 concurrent users, peak 30 qps for short summarization prompts, and batch jobs overnight for longer analytics.
00:51 Rafael: Ok that helps. For open models we typically recommend a shortlist balancing size and quantization profile. Off the top of head: Llama-2-13B-Chat (fine-tuned), Mistral-Instruct-7B, Mosaic MPT-30B-instruct, and Llama-3-8B (if available as an open variant). Each has tradeoffs: 7B is cheaper but sometimes lower quality on finance jargon; 30B gives better coherence but higher cost and memory.
01:12 Maya: We can run all four under Redwood Dedicated or hosted with a dedicated pool for the POC — the main thing is to capture latency/throughput and also run quality evals on your prompt set.
01:22 Priya: For success criteria, we propose: 1) average answer accuracy > 85% on our eval set, 2) p95 latency < 1500ms on targeted config, and 3) cost under $X per 1k tokens — we'll define X after we see the first runs.
01:35 Elena: And quality metrics should include domain-specific metrics: entity extraction precision, numerical accuracy on tables, and hallucination checks.
01:45 Rafael: Sounds reasonable. We'll provide the benchmark harness that collects p50/p95, token counts, and also runs your evaluation prompts to score quality. We'll instrument with Redwood Console traces so you can see per-token cost and KV cache hit rates. Note: transcription sometimes writes KV cache as 'KV cash' in our docs, just ignore that.
02:03 Samir: On infra — for the private deployment option, we need VPC peering and KMS. Are there templates for peering and IP ranges?
02:11 Maya: Yes, we'll send network diagrams and IP ranges. For KMS, we integrate with AWS KMS and customer-managed keys. We'll also include the SOC2 package.
02:20 Priya: Do you support on-prem or air-gapped cases? We have one regulated customer that might ask for air-gap later.
02:25 Rafael: We do via Redwood Private — it's a separate package. For the POC we recommend hosted dedicated or a VPC deployment to keep iteration fast; air-gapped adds ops overhead and slows benchmarks.
02:40 Elena: Back to models — what's your experience with multilingual performance? Mistral vs Llama variants?
02:46 Rafael: Mistral-Instruct-7B is decent for Spanish/Portuguese general tasks but may struggle with finance-specific nomenclature. Llama derivatives (13B or 30B) tend to be stronger after instruction tuning on domain data. If you bring a small domain-tuning set (10-50k tokens), the 13B often hits a good cost/quality sweet spot.
03:05 Priya: Okay that suggests we should run 7B and 13B variants as our primary two, and maybe one 30B as a control. Can Redwood handle mixed routing so we can compare side-by-side?
03:13 Maya: Yes, we can set up a split route for the pilot traffic and automatically gather the metrics per model. We'll also enable automatic fallback to smaller models if capacity is constrained.
03:25 Samir: For workload sizing, Rafael — what batch sizes and GPU types do you recommend for 13B quantized?
03:30 Rafael: For 13B quantized we usually run on A100-40 or an equivalent H100 small slice; with int8 quantization you can get good throughput. We'll include recommended batch sizes in the harness; expect ~40-60 qps for short prompts on Dedicated with a shared pool, but that depends on sequence length.
03:47 Elena: Sequence lengths for our prompts average 120 tokens, responses about 80 tokens. Overnight analytics run sequences ~800-2k tokens but are batchy.
03:55 Rafael: Good, that'll affect memory but not latency for interactive path. We'll simulate both interactive and batch workloads in the harness.
04:06 Priya: Benchmarks: beyond latency and quality, we need cost projections for 6-month scale — do you provide cost model estimates?
04:13 Maya: Yes, Redwood Optimize will give a cost breakdown per model with recommended batching and caching settings. We can provide projected cost curves for the three candidate models using your volume assumptions.
04:24 Elena: About evaluation — Rafael, can you integrate our current unit tests (we have ~150 prompt-answer pairs) into your harness?
04:31 Rafael: Absolutely, we typically take your eval set and run it across models, producing CSVs with precision/recall, hallucination flags, and numerical accuracy checks. We'll flag any consistent regressions.
04:44 Priya: Any blockers from security? We need SSO/SAML and RBAC for our team.
04:50 Maya: SSO via SAML is supported, plus RBAC and audit logs. We'll include a sample role matrix in the doc pack.
04:58 Samir: Timeline — goal to decide model and run first benchmark in 2 weeks. Is that realistic?
05:03 Maya: Yes, if we get sample data and you sign the pilot (standard MSA + DPA), we can spin up a Dedicated pilot pool and run the harness within 10 business days.
05:12 Priya: Sounds good. Let's do: deliverables from Redwood by 9/3, Quantilytics provide data by 9/6, run benchmarks week of 9/13 and review week of 9/13-9/17.
05:24 Rafael: We'll also run a small synthetic load test to validate autoscaling and metrics for p95 tails. One note: open models differ in tokenization which affects token counts; our cost comparisons will normalize for tokenization differences but expect slight variance.
05:40 Elena: Any recommended prompt engineering or system messages for financial extraction?
05:44 Rafael: We'll share a prompt guide; include ways to force numerical extraction and add sanity-check post-processing steps. For tables we recommend structured output or function-calls approach for deterministic parsing.
05:58 Priya: Competitors — we did a quick look at OpenAI and Anthropic; we prefer an open path to avoid vendor lock but we might consider Anthropic if quality on financial LLM tasks is significantly better.
06:12 Maya: Understood. We'll include a short comparison sheet highlighting where open models trade off against hosted incumbents on cost and quality.
06:20 Priya: Ok that's it from my side. Thanks, this was helpful.
06:24 Maya: Great, Rafael and I will follow up with the harness and security docs. Any final questions?
06:29 Samir: None here.
06:31 Elena: Nope.
06:33 Maya: Thanks all, we'll send the follow-ups and calendar invites for the benchmark review.
06:37 Meeting end.

Notes about transcript quality: occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., 'Redwood Dedicated' sometimes typed as 'Redwood dedicate' or 'KV cache' as 'KV cash'). We left filler words and small overlaps to keep it authentic.
